content:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache pager pool on cluster-prod-3 experiencing sustained fragmentation and rising GPU memory pressure (paged-attn allocator). 80% of nodes reporting >75% resident KV pages.
incident-bot: Metric spike started 2024-03-12T01:02:10Z, slow upward trend to OOM risk. Auto-escalation to incidents channel.
sandeep: acked — I'm oncall for runtime, joining. pulling logs now.
mike: looking at node list, 3/12 workers are flapping, a couple container restarts on gpu-12.*
jessica: customer-ops ping: two customers reported increased error rate and degraded latency on embeddings endpoints. K/V loadups for long-running chat sessions.
kelsey-custops: confirmed: support ticket #4682 — customer saw repeated 500s and retries from our hosted API. They’re on a production deploy.
sandeep: initial hypothesis: paged-attention allocator fragmentation + slow KV cache leak when attention paging hits a mixed sequence-length workload. It's creeping memory until CUDA driver forces aborts.
mike: can we push a lighter fallback model variant (lower kv-resident) to affected routes? We have a compatible quantized variant.
sandeep: yes, can reroute chat-prod -> model:ctx-lite-v2 (quantized) for tenanted routes. Will add temporary routing rule.
jessica: doing that now via rollout API. small canary 10% -> 100% if stable.
incident-bot: DEPLOY: rollout started by jessica at 2024-03-12T01:10:45Z. Canary at 10%. Autoplayback set to hold 5m.
mike: also recommend raising page-evict-threshold to avoid hot-resident amplification while we stabilize. Oncall approvals?
oncall-lead: +1 for threshold bump to buy time. Make conservative change.
sandeep: applying evict threshold + throttle for long-lived KV sessions. patch:
```bash
# temporarily lower resident target to force more aggressive eviction
redwoodctl runtime set-param --cluster prod-3 --param kv.evict_threshold=0.55
redwoodctl runtime set-param --cluster prod-3 --param kv.long_session_timeout=900
```
sandeep: changes applied to subset (region-us-west) at 2024-03-12T01:18Z. Monitoring.
jessica: canary metrics: 10% route shows 30% reduction in OOM restarts and 15% lower p95 latency for canary traffic.
kelsey-custops: relaying to customer: we applied a temporary routing and are monitoring, may need brief maintenance if issues persist.
mike: I’m scavenging KV bitmaps to defragment cold pages on the node group; will trigger a rolling drain on two nodes to reclaim resident sets.
sandeep: schedule rolling drain now, 1 node at a time, gracefully migrate sessions. Use drain-label: incident/kv-nightfest.
mike: drain started on gpu-12-1, migrating 24 sessions. ETA ~6m.
incident-bot: NODE-RESTART: gpu-12-1 drained and soft-restart triggered at 2024-03-12T01:33:10Z.
jessica: canary -> 30% now; watching error rate.
kelsey-custops: customer confirmed error rate dropping, still seeing elevated latency for some endpoints.
sandeep: next step: enable KV-cache-prefetch disable for long-tail sessions to reduce KV footprint — flip in 5m if drains look good.
mike: after drain 1 completed, memory pressure dropped ~20% on that AZ. proceeding with second node.
oncall-lead: good progress. Prepare postmortem skeleton and assign initial P0s: root-cause triage (sandeep,mike), mitigations doc (jessica), customer comms (kelsey-custops).
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigations in flight, impact reduced to partial degradation. SLA risk: medium. Next update in 15m or on major change.
sandeep: handing off to next oncall in 2h. leaving runbook notes and current commands in incident board. If creep resumes, escalate to runtime-pager.
jessica: continuing monitoring, will revert routing once stable for 30m.
kelsey-custops: updating affected customers: we’ve implemented a temporary routing and memory-evicting adjustments; full post-incident summary forthcoming.
oncall-lead: thanks team — documented actions, we’ll keep this thread open for the handoff. :)
